screens.title: Chats · Nordic Retail — Lars
screens.caption: A buyer changes a date in a WhatsApp thread. The message is read, the plan is re-scheduled, tasks are created, and the chase to the factory is drafted — before anyone opens the ERP.

screens.title: Today
screens.caption: The merchandiser's morning: what needs a decision, what the system already chased overnight, and which orders are quiet for too long.

screens.title: Rules & ladders · Stage due
screens.caption: A chase ladder per stage, in plain language: who is asked, how, when — and when it stops being polite. The wording is your team's, not a template.

screens.title: Tasks
screens.caption: Nobody writes tasks. They appear from the plan, from messages and from documents — with the reason attached — and close themselves when the evidence arrives.

screens.title: Order · PO 4471
screens.caption: Every chase, reply and re-plan is logged against the order — so when a date is missed, the history of who was asked what, and when, is one click away.

screens.title: Digests
screens.caption: One message every morning per role — what moved, what is stuck, what it costs — compiled from the plans and the chats, not typed by anyone.

screens.title: Factory side · on the phone
screens.caption: Factories don't log in to anything. They reply on WhatsApp, in Hinglish, with a date — and that reply moves the plan.
